mainTopic: How a body shields swallowed items from passing on or receiving טומאה, and why רבה's rule about two swallowed rings is needed
overview: This amud is about items closed up inside a body (בלוע). It opens by finishing a קל וחומר: a person shields swallowed impurity from spreading out, so he should also shield a pure item inside him from becoming impure. The גמרא challenges the comparison to a כלי חרס and defends it, showing that on the inside a כלי חרס is actually stricter. Next it extends the rule to an item that entered the body from below, using a קל וחומר based on digestion. Then it extends the rule from a person to an animal. A challenge from the rules of a בית המנוגע is answered with a משנה about clothes a person carries in. Finally, רבא asks why רבה needed to teach his rule, since two משניות about a swallowed ring already teach both swallowed impurity and swallowed purity. The answer is that רבה was teaching something new: two swallowed rings, one impure and one pure, do not pass impurity to each other.

steps.title: Finishing the logical argument about a person
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא completes a קל וחומר. A person shields impurity inside him from spreading, so he should also shield a pure item inside him from becoming impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person shields impurity that is inside him from making other things impure. Isn't it logical, then, that he also shields a pure item inside him from becoming impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a קל וחומר. The first half, about a כלי חרס, was said just before this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the גמרא showed that impurity swallowed inside a person does not spread out to things around him. Now it argues that the same shield should also work the other way. A pure item inside a person should be protected from impurity outside.

keyTerms.meaning: Shields or protects
Impurity that is inside him
A pure item that is inside him
Isn't it logical? This is the phrase that closes a קל וחומר.
A logical argument: if something is true in a weaker case, it is surely true in a stronger case

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two directions. מִלְּטַמֵּא means stopping impurity from going OUT and making other things impure. מִלִּיטַּמֵּא means stopping the item inside from BECOMING impure.

phrases.english: A person, who shields impurity
phrases.notes: This is impurity a person swallowed, like a piece of a dead body, as the גמרא showed earlier.

phrases.english: that is inside him from making things impure
is it not logical that he shields a pure item
inside him from becoming impure?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁמַּצִּיל עַל טׇהֳרָה שֶׁבְּתוֹכוֹ מִלִּיטַּמֵּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the קל וחומר whose first half, about a כלי חרס, was stated just before.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By קל וחומר, a person shields a pure item inside him from becoming impure.

steps.title: Challenge: a person can become impure from his outside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the comparison. A כלי חרס cannot become impure from its outside, but a person can, so maybe a person is not as protective as a כלי חרס.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is special about a כלי חרס is that it does not become impure from its outside. Can you say the same about a person, who does become impure from his outside?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the קל וחומר. It points out a way that a person is stricter than a כלי חרס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קל וחומר only works if the first case is truly weaker in every relevant way. Here the challenge shows that in one way, a כלי חרס is more resistant to impurity than a person. So we cannot simply move its protective power over to a person.

keyTerms.meaning: What is special about...? This is the classic way to attack a קל וחומר.
An earthenware (clay) vessel
From its back, meaning from its outside
Since, because

phrases.english: What is special about an earthenware vessel?
It does not become impure from its outside.
Will you say the same about a person, who becomes impure from his outside?

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לִכְלִי חֶרֶס, שֶׁכֵּן אֵין מִטַּמֵּא מִגַּבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the קל וחומר of step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison between a כלי חרס and a person in the קל וחומר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A person is stricter than a כלי חרס because he becomes impure from his outside, so a leniency of the כלי חרס cannot be applied to a person.

steps.title: Answer: we are only talking about the inside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the outside does not matter here. The question is about a pure item inside, so we only compare insides.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are we talking about becoming impure from the outside? We are talking about the inside!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the קל וחומר. It says the difference about the outside has nothing to do with our case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The case is about an item inside a person's body, so only how the inside works matters. The fact that a person becomes impure from his outside is a separate matter. On the inside, the comparison to a כלי חרס still holds.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that to say...? It brings up an idea in order to reject it.
Are we saying, are we talking about
From its inside

phrases.english: Is that to say we are talking about its outside?
We are talking about its inside!

steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the comparison to the relevant area (the inside only)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The challenger thought that any way a person is stricter than a כלי חרס would break the קל וחומר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the inside matters for our case, so the difference about the outside is not relevant.

steps.title: On the inside, a כלי חרס is actually stricter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds that on the inside, a כלי חרס is even stricter than a person. It becomes impure just from impurity in its airspace, so the קל וחומר is even stronger.
steps.simpleTranslation: On the contrary, a כלי חרס is stricter, since it becomes impure through its airspace.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא strengthens its answer. It shows that inside, a כלי חרס is stricter than a person, not more lenient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כלי חרס becomes impure when impurity is just in the empty space inside it, even without touching it. A person becomes impure from something inside him only if it actually touches him. So if even the stricter כלי חרס protects what is inside, a person surely does, and the קל וחומר stands.

keyTerms.meaning: On the contrary
Strict, more severe
From its airspace, the empty space inside it

steps.whatToRemember: The קל וחומר survives. On the inside, a כלי חרס is stricter than a person because it becomes impure from its airspace. So if a כלי חרס protects a pure item inside it, a person surely protects a pure item inside him.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how to defend a קל וחומר. You show that the challenge is about an area that does not matter here, and that in the area that does matter, the comparison works even better.

phrases.english: On the contrary, an earthenware vessel is stricter,
since it becomes impure through its airspace.
phrases.notes: Impurity just hanging in the empty space inside the clay vessel makes it impure, even without touching it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 3 by showing the inside of a כלי חרס is stricter, which makes the קל וחומר stronger.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reversal: the supposed weaker case is actually stricter in the relevant area
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think a person is generally stricter than a כלי חרס.
steps.terutzMaskana: On the inside, a כלי חרס is stricter, so the קל וחומר is valid: a person protects a pure item inside him.

steps.title: What about something that entered the body from below?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא has a source for an impure item swallowed through the mouth. It asks how we know the same rule for an item that entered from below.
steps.simpleTranslation: We found a source for an item swallowed from above, through the mouth. How do we know the rule for an item taken in from below?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a new question. It has a source for an impure item swallowed through the mouth, and now wants a source for one that entered from below.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the discussion was about something swallowed normally, from above. The גמרא wants to know whether the body also protects when the impure item came in from below. This question sets up a new קל וחומר in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Swallowed; an item closed up inside a body
Above; entering through the mouth
Below; entering through the lower opening of the body
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: We found [a source for] an item swallowed from above;
phrases.notes: From above means through the mouth. The גמרא already proved this case earlier.

phrases.english: an item taken in from below, from where do we know?
phrases.notes: From below means it entered through the rectum.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחַן בָּלוּעַ דִּלְמַעְלָה, בָּלוּעַ דִּלְמַטָּה מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After securing the basic rule, the גמרא extends it to a new case: entry from below.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that an impure item that entered the body from below is also shielded.

steps.title: קל וחומר: below digests, so it surely protects
steps.stepSummary: The upper part of the body does not digest, yet it protects. The lower part does digest, so it should surely protect.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a קל וחומר. The upper part does not digest food, and still it protects. The lower part does digest food, so surely it protects.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a קל וחומר. If the mouth area protects even though it does not digest, then the lower area, which does digest, should protect even more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The measuring stick here is digestion, עיכול. The upper part does not digest, yet it still protects. The lower part does digest, so it should be at least as protective as the upper part.

keyTerms.meaning: Digestion
Protects; shields the item from spreading טומאה
Is it not logical? The closing phrase of a קל וחומר

phrases.english: [It is derived by] a קל וחומר: if above,
which does not digest, protects,
then below, which does digest,
is it not logical that it protects?

steps.triggerLanguage: קַל וָחוֹמֶר: וּמָה לְמַעְלָה, שֶׁאֵינוֹ עוֹשֶׂה עִיכּוּל
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קל וחומר from the upper part, which does not digest, to the lower part, which does.

steps.title: Lower digestion depends on the upper part
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the קל וחומר: the lower part only digests because of the work the upper part already did.
steps.simpleTranslation: But does the lower part digest at all, except because of the upper part?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the קל וחומר. It points out that digestion below only happens because of what the upper part did first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר said the lower part is "stronger" because it digests. The challenge says that strength really belongs to the upper part. If so, the lower part is not truly stronger, and the קל וחומר breaks down.

keyTerms.meaning: Does it at all? (a challenging question word)
By means of; because of

phrases.english: Does digestion happen below at all
except by means of above?
phrases.notes: He means the chewing and early digestion done in the upper part of the body.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּלוּם עוֹשֶׂה עִיכּוּל לְמַטָּה אֶלָּא עַל יְדֵי מַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the premise of the קל וחומר in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 6 that the lower part is stronger because it digests.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Digestion below depends on the upper part, so the lower part is not independently stronger.

steps.title: Still, digestion below is greater
steps.stepSummary: Even if it depends on the upper part, more digestion happens below, so the קל וחומר stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even so, the digestion below is greater.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Even if the lower part needs the upper part, the lower part still does more digesting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer agrees that the upper part helps, but says that does not matter. What counts is that more digestion actually takes place below. So the lower part is still "stronger," and the קל וחומר holds.

keyTerms.meaning: Even so
Great; greater (here not a person's name)

steps.whatToRemember: The body shields a swallowed impure item whether it entered from above or from below, because digestion below is even greater.
steps.confusionAlert: The word רַב here means "greater," not the sage named רב.

phrases.english: Even so, the digestion below is greater.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7 and keeps the קל וחומר of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Concedes the fact but denies it matters
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since digestion below depends on the upper part, the lower part is not stronger.
steps.terutzMaskana: Whatever the cause, more digestion happens below, so the lower part is stronger and protects.

steps.title: What about something swallowed by an animal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא has the rule for a person and asks how we know it for an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: We found the rule for an item swallowed by a person. How do we know the rule for an item swallowed by an animal?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a second extension. It asks whether an animal's body also shields an impure item it swallowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything so far was about a human body. Now the גמרא asks whether an animal's body works the same way. This sets up another קל וחומר in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: We found (a source)
Animal

phrases.english: We found [a source for] an item swallowed by a person;
an item swallowed by an animal, from where do we know?

steps.triggerLanguage: אַשְׁכְּחַן בָּלוּעַ דְּאָדָם, בָּלוּעַ דִּבְהֵמָה מְנָלַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the from-below case, the גמרא extends the rule from people to animals.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that an animal's body also shields a swallowed impure item.

steps.title: קל וחומר: an animal is purer than a person
steps.stepSummary: A person can make things impure while alive and still protects. An animal cannot make things impure while alive, so it should surely protect.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a קל וחומר. A person can become a source of טומאה while alive, and still he protects a swallowed item. An animal does not cause טומאה while alive, so surely it protects a swallowed item.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a קל וחומר. A living animal is "cleaner" than a person, so if a person protects, an animal should protect even more.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A living person can spread טומאה, for example as a זב or a מצורע, while a living animal never does. If even the person, who is more open to טומאה, keeps the swallowed item in, then an animal, which is less open to it, should surely do the same.

keyTerms.meaning: Becomes a source of טומאה while still alive
In the case of a swallowed item

phrases.english: [It is derived by] a קל וחומר: if a person,
who becomes impure while alive, protects a swallowed item,
then an animal, which does not cause impurity while alive,
is it not logical that it protects a swallowed item?

steps.triggerLanguage: קַל וָחוֹמֶר: וּמָה אָדָם שֶׁמִּטַּמֵּא מֵחַיִּים מַצִּיל בְּבָלוּעַ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A קל וחומר from a person, who can be impure while alive, to an animal, which cannot.

steps.title: In a leprous house, an animal is stricter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the קל וחומר. In a בית המנוגע, a person must stay a while before his clothes become impure, but an animal does not need to stay. So an animal is stricter in at least one way.
steps.simpleTranslation: What about a person? He is special because he needs to stay a while in a בית המנוגע. Can you say the same about an animal, which does not need to stay a while in a בית המנוגע?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the קל וחומר. It shows a case where an animal is stricter than a person, so we cannot assume an animal is always "cleaner."
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who walks into a בית המנוגע makes his clothes impure only if he stays long enough. An animal that walks in makes what it carries impure right away. Since the animal is stricter here, maybe it is stricter about a swallowed item too, so the קל וחומר is weakened. The next step answers this challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: What about...? The opening of a challenge that shows a weak point in a קל וחומר
Staying; remaining for a set amount of time
A house struck with צרעת (leprosy)
Can you say? (that the same applies to the other case)

steps.confusionAlert: The stay applies to the person's clothes. A person entering a בית המנוגע becomes impure himself right away; the stay is only needed before his clothes become impure.

phrases.english: What about a person?
He is special because he needs to stay a while in a leprous house,
phrases.notes: He has to stay a while before his clothes become impure. See ויקרא 14.

phrases.english: can you say [the same] about an animal,
which does not need to stay a while in a leprous house?
phrases.notes: Anything an animal carries in becomes impure right away, with no waiting.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה לְאָדָם, שֶׁכֵּן צָרִיךְ שְׁהִיָּיה בְּבַיִת הַמְנוּגָּע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the קל וחומר of step 10 by showing an area where an animal is stricter than a person.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption in step 10 that an animal is always more lenient than a person regarding טומאה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In a בית המנוגע an animal is stricter than a person, so a leniency of a person cannot simply be carried over to an animal.

steps.title: The animal's 'stricter' rule is really the same for a person
steps.stepSummary: The animal's rule of not needing to stay in a בית המנוגע only applies to utensils on its back, and a person carrying utensils on his back is treated the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: An animal doesn't need to stay in a בית המנוגע. What law does that teach? It is about the utensils on its back. But a person doesn't need to stay for that either!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 11. The animal is not really stricter than a person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A live animal can never become impure itself, so 'it needs no waiting time' can only be about the utensils it carries. A person carrying utensils on his back also makes them impure right away. So there is no real difference, and the קל וחומר from person to animal is back in place.

keyTerms.meaning: A house struck with צרעת. Entering it makes a person or object impure.
Staying or waiting for a certain amount of time.
For what law? What practical difference does it make?

phrases.english: An animal, which does not need to stay
in a house struck with צרעת
for what law does that matter?
phrases.notes: A live animal itself can't become impure, so the waiting rule can't be about the animal's own body.

phrases.english: For utensils that are on its back.
A person also does not need to stay for that!

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּהֵמָה דְּאֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה שְׁהִיָּיה בְּבַיִת הַמְנוּגָּע, לְמַאי הִלְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11 by narrowing what the animal's 'no waiting' rule is really about.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the supposed stricter rule applies equally to people.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: An animal seemed stricter than a person in a בית המנוגע, which would break the קל וחומר.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule is only about carried utensils, and those become impure right away with a person too, so the קל וחומר stands.

steps.title: Proof from the משנה about entering a house struck with צרעת
steps.stepSummary: A משנה shows that clothes and objects a person carries (not wears) become impure at once, just like the utensils on an animal's back.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: someone who enters a בית המנוגע with his clothes on his shoulders and his sandals and rings in his hands becomes impure right away, and so do they. If he was wearing his clothes, with sandals on his feet and rings on his finger, he becomes impure right away. But they stay pure until he stays as long as it takes to eat a פרס: wheat bread, not barley bread, eaten reclining with something to dip it in.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה to prove what it just said: carried items become impure immediately, even when a person brings them in.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה separates carried items from worn items. Items carried in the hands or on the shoulders become impure at once, the same as utensils on an animal's back. Only worn items get the waiting time, and that is an extra leniency for people. It does not make animals stricter.

keyTerms.meaning: The time it takes to eat a פרס, half a loaf of bread.
Reclining while eating.
A relish or side dish eaten with bread.

steps.confusionAlert: The person himself becomes impure right away in both cases. The waiting time is only for the clothes and objects he is wearing.

phrases.english: As we learned: one who enters a house struck with צרעת
with his clothes on his shoulders
and his sandals and his rings in his hands
he and they are impure immediately.
If he was wearing his clothes
and his sandals were on his feet
and his rings were on his finger
he is impure immediately,
but they are pure until he stays
for the time it takes to eat a half-loaf,
wheat bread and not barley bread,
phrases.notes: Wheat bread is eaten faster, so the waiting time is shorter.

phrases.english: reclining and eating it with a relish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for step 12's claim that a person's carried items become impure right away.
steps.raayaObject: Utensils carried by a person (not worn) become impure immediately in a בית המנוגע.

steps.title: רבא: both swallowed-item rules are already in a משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks why רבה's rule was needed, since both swallowed impurity and swallowed purity are already taught in משניות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: We already learned both of them. We learned the rule of swallowed impurity, and we learned the rule of swallowed purity!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic. רבא asks why רבה had to state his rule about swallowed items, since a משנה already teaches both parts. This step sets up the sources that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה taught that an impure item swallowed inside a body cannot make things impure, and a pure item inside a body cannot become impure. רבא says both halves already appear in משניות, so רבה's statement seems to teach nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: A swallowed (enclosed) impure item. It cannot pass on impurity while it is inside.
A swallowed (enclosed) pure item. It cannot become impure while it is inside.
We already learned both of them in a משנה.

phrases.english: רבא said: We learned both of them,
phrases.notes: He's pointing back to רבה's rule about swallowed items from earlier on the דף.

phrases.english: swallowed impurity, we learned it;
swallowed purity, we learned it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the קל וחומר discussion and goes back to רבה's earlier rule about swallowed items.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's statement about טומאה בלועה and טהרה בלועה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both rules are already in a משנה, an אמורא does not need to state them.

steps.title: Source for swallowed impurity: the swallowed ring
steps.stepSummary: A משנה rules that a person who swallowed an impure ring can immerse and eat תרומה, but if he vomits it up, it makes him impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Swallowed impurity, as we learned: If he swallowed an impure ring, he immerses and eats his תרומה. If he vomited it up, it is impure and it makes him impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings his first source, a משנה showing that an impure item inside a body cannot pass impurity to the person while it stays inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ring is still impure inside him, yet after immersing he may eat תרומה, so while it is swallowed it cannot pass on impurity. Once it comes out it is still impure and makes him impure again. This is exactly רבה's rule of טומאה בלועה.

keyTerms.meaning: Immerses in a מקוה to become pure.
The portion given to a כהן. It may only be eaten in a state of purity.
He vomited it up.

phrases.english: Swallowed impurity, as we learned:
If he swallowed an impure ring,
he immerses and eats his תרומה,
phrases.notes: The ring is still inside him, yet it doesn't stop him from becoming pure.

phrases.english: if he vomited it up, it is impure, and it made him impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first of the two sources רבא promised in step 14.
steps.raayaObject: An impure item inside a body cannot pass on impurity.

steps.title: A swallowed pure ring stays pure
steps.stepSummary: רבא finishes his challenge: the rule of טהרה בלועה (a swallowed pure item) is also already taught in a משנה. A pure ring swallowed before entering a tent with a dead body comes out still pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: We also learned about swallowed purity, as the משנה says: If someone swallowed a pure ring, then went into a tent with a dead body, was sprinkled on the third and seventh days, immersed, and then vomited up the ring, the ring is just as it was (pure).
steps.whatsHappening: רבא brings the second half of his proof. Just as swallowed impurity is already in a משנה, swallowed purity is too, so what did רבה add?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ring was inside the person's body when he became impure in the אהל המת. Since the ring was swallowed, the impurity could not reach it, so it comes out pure. This seems to cover רבה's rule, which makes the challenge stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: A pure item that is swallowed inside a body
A tent or roofed space that holds a dead body, which makes everything inside it impure
He sprinkled and sprinkled again: the red heifer water put on an impure person on the 3rd and 7th days
He vomited it up

phrases.english: Swallowed purity, we have also learned,
as we learned in a משנה: If he swallowed a pure ring,
and then entered a tent with a dead body,
and was sprinkled, and sprinkled again, and immersed,
phrases.notes: This is the full purification for impurity from a dead body: red heifer water on day three and day seven, then immersion.

phrases.english: and then vomited it up, it is just as it was.
phrases.notes: The ring stays pure. The impurity from the dead body never reached it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of רבא's proof, matching step 15 (swallowed impurity) with swallowed purity
steps.raayaObject: That the law of טהרה בלועה is already known from a משנה, so רבה's rule seems unnecessary
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in מקואות (10:8): a swallowed pure ring stays pure even when its swallower became impure from a dead body

steps.title: רבה meant two rings swallowed together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבה was teaching a new case: someone swallowed two rings, one impure and one pure. Even inside the body, the impure ring does not make the pure ring impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבה said his rule, he was talking about a case where someone swallowed two rings, one impure and one pure. The impure ring does not make the pure ring impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רבא's question by showing that רבה's rule covers a case the משנה does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only deals with the ring and the body: the body does not pass impurity to the ring, and the ring does not pass it to the body. רבה adds that two items swallowed together also cannot pass impurity to each other, even if they touch. So his rule is new and needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Two rings
Does not make impure

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה teaches that swallowed items and the body do not pass impurity to each other. רבה adds that two swallowed items do not pass impurity to each other either.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רבה is repeating the משנה. The משנה is about a ring and the body. רבה is about one ring and another ring, both inside the body.

phrases.english: When רבה said his rule,
it was about a case where he swallowed two rings,
one impure and one pure,
that the impure one does not make the pure one impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's challenge from steps 14 to 16
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits רבה's rule to a case the משנה does not cover
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבה's rule just repeats the משנה about one swallowed ring
steps.terutzMaskana: רבה teaches that two swallowed items do not pass impurity to each other, something the משנה does not say
